judge: Claude Code subagent, Claude Opus 5.5, fresh

items.label: A
items.critique: Clean, well-built briefing with a gift of scrolls and a person who will open the gate, but 'besieged in all but name' and 'darker days than this' are a literary polish Westwood's openings rarely have.

items.label: B
items.critique: Clipped, half-finished instructions ('You'll know. And careful.') and a reminder that repeats itself; the slightly awkward plainness is Westwood's.

items.label: C
items.critique: Practical, spell-by-spell advice and 'Good luck and good speed' read like real in-mission guidance; the uneven register ('This may get very ugly, lad') is true to Nox.

items.label: D
items.critique: 'So [Person] sent you. Good.' plus 'By the authority of the [Group], I deputate you' and the 'Why are you still standing in my hall?' reminder follow the same template as several others here; the coined 'deputate' is a misfire.

items.label: E
items.critique: Stiff, expository introduction ('I am [Person]. The Master for the [Place].'), capitalised YOU and a fragment-heavy reminder: rough edges a pastiche would smooth away.

items.label: F
items.critique: Vivid, controlled scene-setting (screaming heard all the way to town, 'the drowned answer to him now') with 'By the authorization of this village, I command you' is the same formula as D and G; too composed for Westwood.

items.label: G
items.critique: Long, rhetorical briefing with a heroic sword gift and a slogan ending ('[Place]'s fires are in your hands!'); the repetition for effect ('every one!') and the tidy stakes are a modern writer's.

items.label: H
items.critique: Breathless, exclamation-laden, slightly ungrammatical ('leaving rebuilding the village our smallest concern') with direct directions (northeast): unmistakably Westwood.

items.label: I
items.critique: Wordy, slightly bureaucratic mentor speech ('Wildlife incursions in the settled areas is on a steady rise') with its grammar slip and a stray empty page: authentic campaign text.

items.label: J
items.critique: Short and plain, closer to Nox than the others, but the same 'So [Person] sent you. Good.' opener and a too-complete journal entry with full location mark it as the template.

tells: The new texts share one opening template ('So, [Person] sent you. Good.') and one closing beat (gift, then 'Go!'), while Westwood's openings vary in shape and often start mid-situation.
New texts frame the order formally ('By the authority of...', 'I command you', 'I deputate you'); Westwood's givers just say what to do.
New texts are more literary and controlled (figurative stakes, rhetorical repetition, slogan endings); Westwood's are plainer, clumsier, with grammar slips, odd capitals and run-on exclamations.
Westwood's briefings carry concrete mechanics (spells to use, which direction, where the key opens); the new ones dwell on the villain's menace instead.
New reminders are all impatient one-liners of the same mould ('Still here?', 'Why are you still standing...'); Westwood's reminders restate the task or add a hint.
